reference: GNU diff for parity cases; Bash type/help metadata and the documented CLI contract for the metadata case.
coverage: Bash builtin/help availability and the documented --version operation.
Equal files, POSIX normal edit scripts, and unified output with three lines of context.
Quiet and case-insensitive comparisons, including their exit statuses.
Missing final newlines and binary input containing NUL bytes.
Both stdin operand positions, differing stdin, diff - -, and preservation of unread stdin.
Leading-dash relative filenames with --, missing-file diagnostics, and invalid-option status.
exclusions: GNU directory comparison and options outside the documented -u/-q/-i, --, and stdin subset are not asserted.
Unified output uses a deliberate GNU --label adapter for the documented filename-only header contract. Raw timestamped GNU headers differ by design and are not claimed as equal.

Repeated-record minimal-edit replay, allocation-failure injection, output-write failure recovery, and low-memory recovery need dedicated generated or fault-injection fixtures and remain outside this compact declarative suite.

cases.purpose: Check Bash metadata and the documented help and version entry points without relying on an external command.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t diff)
if help diff > help.out && [[ -s help.out ]]; then help_state=available; else help_state=missing; fi
if diff --version > version.out && [[ -s version.out ]]; then version_state=available; else version_state=missing; fi
printf 'kind=%s\nhelp=%s\nversion=%s\n' "$kind" "$help_state" "$version_state"

cases.purpose: Identical byte-for-byte text files produce no output and status zero.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha
beta
' > left
printf 'alpha
beta
' > right
diff left right

cases.purpose: Exercise a leading insertion, an interior deletion, and a later replacement whose normal diff addresses depend on preceding edits.
cases.script:
printf 'a
b
c
d
' > left
printf 'x
a
c
y
' > right
diff left right

cases.purpose: Compare every byte of the documented filename-only unified output against GNU diff with explicit labels. The deliberate reference adapter asks GNU for those headers; no output bytes or timestamps are removed.
cases.script:
printf 'first
old
middle
last
' > left
printf 'first
new
middle
last
' > right
if [[ $(type -t diff) == builtin ]]; then
  diff -u left right
else
  diff -u --label left --label right left right
fi

cases.purpose: Quiet mode reports differing relative filenames without a content script and returns the difference status.
cases.script:
printf 'old\n' > left
printf 'new\n' > right
diff -q left right

cases.purpose: Combined -qi flags treat ASCII case-only line differences as equal under the runner's C locale.
cases.script:
printf 'ALPHA\n' > left
printf 'alpha\n' > right
diff -qi left right

cases.purpose: A final-newline-only difference remains visible and carries the standard no-newline marker.
cases.script:
printf 'prefix
old' > left
printf 'prefix
new
' > right
diff left right

cases.purpose: Different files with NUL bytes in the initial probe block use GNU diff's binary diagnostic instead of a text edit script.
cases.script:
printf 'prefix\000old\n' > left
printf 'prefix\000new\n' > right
diff left right

cases.purpose: Check changed stdin as the first operand, equal stdin in both operand positions, and that diff - - leaves the supplied descriptor unread.
cases.script:
printf 'same\n' > input
if diff - input <<< 'other'; then printf 'stdin-left-status=0\n'; else rc=$?; printf 'stdin-left-status=%s\n' "$rc"; fi
diff - input <<< 'same'
diff input - <<< 'same'
exec 3<<<'retained'
diff - - <&3
IFS= read -r remaining <&3
printf 'remaining=%s\n' "$remaining"
exec 3<&-

cases.purpose: The -- option terminator allows comparison of two relative filenames beginning with a dash.
A missing relative operand is an error with status two and a diagnostic; wording is allowed to follow each implementation.
An unsupported option is rejected with usage status two and a diagnostic.
cases.script:
printf 'same\n' > left
printf 'same\n' > right
diff --definitely-invalid left right

cases.purpose: An empty left operand and an unterminated right record produce the GNU insertion script and newline marker.
cases.script:
: > left
printf 'one\ntwo' > right
diff left right
